html:
A fisherman from Galilee named Simon, who became the leading follower of Jesus. Jesus gave him the name Peter, from the Greek for "rock". The gospels show him as the first of the twelve apostles: quick to speak, quick to act, and the one who denied knowing Jesus on the night of his arrest.

After the crucifixion he led the first followers in Jerusalem. The Book of Acts has him preaching there, then travelling the coast to Lydda, Joppa and Caesarea, where he baptised a Roman officer, one of the first non-Jews to join. He later went to Antioch, where he clashed with Paul over whether Jewish and non-Jewish believers could eat together.

Early Christian writers say he ended his life in Rome, and was crucified there under Nero after the Great Fire of 64, upside down by his own request. The route he took to Rome is not recorded.

The bishops of Rome came to claim his authority, and the Catholic Church counts him as the first pope. St Peter's Basilica stands over the place where tradition puts his grave.
